component.name: Herdr
component.summary: Terminals and coding agents in one window

description.p: This is a community package of Herdr, maintained independently. It repackages the official upstream Linux build unmodified and adds Claude Code, and git for the git panel.

Herdr is a desktop window for terminals and coding agents. This package bundles herdr-core, which runs the terminals, so everything runs inside the Flatpak sandbox with no access to host commands. Terminals only see what the sandbox allows and may end when Herdr exits.
Usage telemetry is on by default, as upstream ships it. Turn it off in Settings, Privacy.

Claude Code runs as claude in any terminal. It is downloaded from Anthropic when this package is installed, and updates with the package, not by itself. It comes with the herdr-app and herdr-core skills, installed into ~/.claude/skills when missing.

Terminals run bash, with history kept between sessions. ~/.local and ~/.claude (Claude's settings and login) are persisted so they survive restarts and updates, unless you grant home access below, which makes them your real home directory's.

To add tools to the PATH or customize the prompt, point herdr-core at your own rcfile in ~/.var/app/dev.herdr.app/config/herdr-core/config.toml (~/.config/herdr-core inside the app, like ~/.config/herdr-app): shell = ["/usr/bin/bash", "--rcfile", "/var/config/herdr-core/bashrc"]. Create that file first (~/.var/app/dev.herdr.app/config/herdr-core/bashrc on the host), or bash prints an error in every new terminal. In it, for example: export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH".
The file panel and git info read the folders your terminals are in, which needs access to your files. It is not granted by default; enable it with "flatpak override":
